title: Gimbal hoops in a flat bay

extra.summary: Gimbal hoops lie in the back plane at rest: S1 = ring about +x (back normal) driven 4:1 by a flat AK70 and belt, S2 = inner hoop about an in-plane diameter driven direct by a second AK70 riding on the ring, S3 XM540 on the hoop, arm along the hoop plane. Flat at rest, but the tilting hoop sweeps a sphere of R 44 about P, so the real envelope is not much flatter than a 'dome <= 40 mm'.

axes.S1: ring axis +x (back normal) through P=(-30,0,0), AK70 #1 flat on the plate at (y 15, z -118), belt 4:1
axes.S2: in-plane diameter A2=(0,cos phi,-sin phi) through P, AK70 #2 on the ring, direct drive
axes.S3: arm axis (in the hoop plane), XM540 on the hoop

ranges_deg.hard_stops: 5 deg beyond, passive (ring stop lugs on the fixed arc; hoop stop lugs on the ring)

extra.unreachable: none inside the box; the box also reaches more directions than the baseline (forward-horizontal at theta 80, backward-down region is not needed)

P.vs_baseline: P moves 30 mm toward the body (x 0 -> -30); head/neck keep-out tables shift

torque.S2_unbalanced: tau_S2 = M sin(theta) cos(phi), M = 6.49 N.m worst: 6.49 N.m vs 8.3 rated = SF 1.28 (same as baseline, FAIL < 2)
torque.S2_balancer: balancer fixed to the ring cannot know phi: K = M/2 = 3.25 N.m, residual max|M cos(phi) - K| sin(80) = 3.20 N.m -> SF 2.60 (PASS) over phi -40..90
torque.S1: arm horizontal, theta 0: 6.49 + S2 motor 0.621 kg x 9.81 x 0.085 m = 0.52 -> 7.0 N.m at the ring; motor torque = 7.0/(4.0 x 0.92) = 1.9 N.m -> SF 4.4; belt tension F = (7.0/4)/0.0155 m = 113 N (belt rating PLACEHOLDER)
torque.speed: S1 joint speed cap 49.5 deg/s -> 198 deg/s at the motor shaft (4:1), AK70 speed limit PLACEHOLDER

extra.stops: passive: S1 ring lugs on the fixed arc; S2 lugs between hoop pivot boss and ring; TPU bumpers at +5 deg beyond soft
extra.balancer: K sin(theta) cord/sheave or clockspring at the passive +A2 pivot between ring and hoop, K = 3.2 N.m (half the worst, see torque)
extra.wiring: S2 motor and S3 bundle (8.2 mm) leave the ring through a flex loop along the ring face; total phi travel 130 deg so no slip ring; the hoop pivot has no hollow shaft so S3/E cables run in a loop along the hoop edge
decision_conflicts: ball-styled shoulder / concurrent axes: axes stay concurrent but the ball is gone (Forest override)
arm rest direction changes: rest is in the back plane, not up (control homology map and keep-out tables change)
S1 now carries gravity (baseline S1 was vertical, no load)
contract_changes: plate shrinks to 94-88 mm and moves 6 mm rearward, outline z -165..-58; S1 4 x M5 block pattern replaced by the rib/arc standoffs
clasp feet and wing tongue seats unchanged in y,z but the plate x face moves from -88 to -94 (wing lap +6 mm)
pros: flat at rest (ring plane 28 mm thick, fairing 82 mm incl. motors)
concurrent axes, same actuators, SF 4.4 on S1 via the belt
ranges cover 100 % of the baseline direction set
cons: swept hoop sphere R44 about P: no flat dome, depth to +158 mm behind back over the range
S2 SF 1.28 without a balancer, balancer cannot track phi (residual 3.25 N.m)
ring needs >= 180 deg of retention but the S2 motor orbit blocks 90..220 deg of the track: bearing is UNRESOLVED (a segmented race is a PLACEHOLDER)
exposed pinch points between hoop and ring (ISO 13857 4 mm rule) need a guard
risks: ring/hoop alignment tolerance, belt stretch (backlash at the tip: 0.5 deg ring = 5 mm at 575 mm)
S2 motor mass on the ring (0.52 N.m on S1)
head clearance with P 30 mm closer
assumptions: rated 8.3 N.m, belt efficiency 0.92, belt/bearing/pulley vendor parts PLACEHOLDER
arm stub = upper arm to the elbow ball only

mass_table_g.note: structure+armour 934 g vs baseline mount proxy 565.6 g

extra.skin_gap_note: plate min skin gap 17.5 mm (< 20 mm over the moving blade rule: trim the plate lower edge or raise it 3 mm); all other parts >= 32 mm; hoop/S2 motor at the display pose >= 65 mm
extra.depth_note: depth at display pose 122 mm, swept over the S1/S2 box 158 mm (baseline 181, -13 % swept / -32 % displayed); the 40 mm dome is NOT achieved: the hoop sphere R44 about P needs P_x + 44 = +14 mm.
